system_description.narrative_title: Bond selloff from sticky inflation and oil-driven rate fears
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is that global government bond yields are surging as sticky inflation readings and a jump in oil push markets to price more central-bank rate hikes. Market interventions (notably Scott Bessent's large Treasury buyback) have so far failed to stop the repricing, highlighting limited short-term control by policy or fiscal actors. This is an open system: exogenous shocks (oil, geopolitics, CPI prints) feed expectations, which drive yields that in turn tighten financial conditions and feed back into growth and inflation prospects.
system_description.scope: Within the system: government bond markets (US Treasuries, Bunds, JGBs), inflation data and expectations, energy (oil) price shock, central-bank policy expectations and rate decisions (Fed, ECB, BOJ), market interventions (Treasury buybacks), and the immediate transmission to equities, gold and FX.
system_description.super_system: Global macroeconomic and financial system (monetary policy, international trade, and real economic activity)
adjacent_subsystems: Energy markets (oil producers, prices, and supply shocks)
Equity markets (risk asset valuations and flows)
Banking/credit and regulatory actions (sanctions, bank health, liquidity)

variables.name: Headline inflation rate
variables.description: The measured overall consumer price inflation rate including volatile items such as energy and food.

variables.name: Core inflation rate
variables.description: Consumer price inflation excluding volatile components, representing underlying inflation momentum.

variables.name: Inflation expectations
variables.description: The market and public's expected future inflation path over relevant horizons.

variables.name: Oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price level for crude oil as a broad energy-price indicator.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: The magnitude and frequency of short-term fluctuations in oil prices.

variables.name: Long-term government bond yield
variables.description: The prevailing market yield on long-dated sovereign bonds representing the cost of long-term government borrowing.

variables.name: Term premium level
variables.description: The component of long-term yields that compensates investors for interest-rate and reinvestment risk over the term.

variables.name: Short-term policy rate
variables.description: The current short-term policy interest rate set by monetary authorities that anchors overnight borrowing costs.

variables.name: Policy rate expectations
variables.description: The market-implied expected future path of short-term policy rates over coming policy cycles.

variables.name: Market intervention intensity
variables.description: The rate and scale of active market-support operations (e.g., asset purchases or buybacks) implemented to influence market prices.

variables.name: Bond market liquidity
variables.description: The ease, depth and breadth with which bonds can be transacted without large price impact.

variables.name: Financial conditions
variables.description: A composite measure of overall financial tightness including rates, spreads, credit availability and volatility.

variables.name: Credit spread level
variables.description: The average difference between corporate borrowing yields and sovereign yields reflecting credit risk premia.

variables.name: Equity market valuation
variables.description: The prevailing valuation metric of equity markets (e.g., aggregate price-to-earnings) reflecting price relative to fundamentals.

variables.name: Exchange rate level
variables.description: The prevailing value of the currency exchange rate relevant to the system (e.g., broad trade-weighted or a major bilateral rate).

variables.name: Real growth expectations
variables.description: The expected path of real economic activity or GDP growth over the medium term.
